successCriteria.description: The 'Request leave' link (accessible name 'Request leave', href '/leaves/new') is rendered while the list is in the loading state — i.e. when `leaveService.list()` has not yet resolved and the component shows its loading indicator.

The 'Request leave' link (accessible name 'Request leave', href '/leaves/new') is rendered while the list is in the error state — i.e. when `leaveService.list()` rejects and the component shows its error alert.

The 'Request leave' link remains rendered in the empty and populated states (existing behavior preserved) — the link is present regardless of which of the four list states (loading/error/empty/populated) is active.

constraints: The link must be rendered outside the loading/error/empty/populated conditional so it is present in all four states; it must not be moved inside any early return or conditional branch.
The existing list rendering (loading indicator, error alert, empty message, populated list) must remain intact and unchanged in behavior.
The link must continue to use react-router-dom's `Link` to `/leaves/new` (the already-registered route); no new route registration is required.
outOfScope: No change to the RequestLeavePage form, the /leaves/new route registration, or the composition root wiring — those are already delivered and out of scope for this phase.
No change to the list data-fetching logic, error handling, or the rendering of the loading/error/empty/populated states themselves.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The link's target path must match the already-registered route `/leaves/new` in the composition root (App.tsx), which renders RequestLeavePage inside RequireAuth.
The link's accessible name and href must match the existing test assertion ('Request leave' → '/leaves/new') so the existing test continues to pass unchanged.
The page must keep consuming `ILeaveService.list()` (returning `Promise<LeaveRequestView[]>`) as its data source; no new service method or interface change is introduced by this phase.
